fixes.explanation: A ram, friend? That would make for a pushy errand. Jesus says they'll find a colt tied there as soon as they enter the village (Mark 11:2). A colt is what He names, so a colt is what they go looking for.
True, friend. Jesus calls it a colt "…on which no one has ever sat." (Mark 11:2) A colt with no riding miles on it at all. I know a thing or two about being well used, and this colt is the opposite.

Not quite, baker. Jesus does say it, in His own words: a colt "…on which no one has ever sat." (Mark 11:2) So the statement is true, and the colt has never had a rider. It's right there in His instructions.

Good thinking, baker, but that's not the line. Jesus tells them to say, "The Lord needs it and will return it shortly." (Mark 11:3) Paying somebody back is a different thing from returning the colt. And nothing about tonight. The words He hands them are the words they use.

Not false, friend. The text says they led the colt to Jesus and threw their cloaks over it, "…and He sat on it." (Mark 11:7) The colt that no one had ever sat on now has Jesus on it. So the answer is True.

Branches, baker! Others in the crowd spread "…branches they had cut from the fields." (Mark 11:8) Many in the crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others spread the branches. Cloaks and branches, all laid down on the road.

Grain sounds like a field thing, I'll give you that. But the text says others spread "…branches they had cut from the fields." (Mark 11:8) Grain isn't what Mark names. Branches are the answer, and many also spread their cloaks on the road.
Straw is a good field guess, friend. But Mark says others spread "…branches they had cut from the fields." (Mark 11:8) Straw isn't mentioned. Many also spread their cloaks on the road.

David, baker! The crowd shouts, "Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!" (Mark 11:10) David was made king over Israel (2 Samuel 5:3), and the crowd calls him "our father." The ones who went ahead and those who followed were all shouting.
Abraham is a big name, friend, but he's not the one in this shout. The crowd shouts, "Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!" (Mark 11:10) The kingdom they name is David's.

Jacob is a good guess, baker, but he's not the name in this shout. The crowd cries, "Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!" (Mark 11:10) David was made king over Israel (2 Samuel 5:3), and it's his kingdom they bless.
True, baker. Jesus entered Jerusalem "…and went into the temple courts." (Mark 11:11) After the shouting on the road, that's where He goes. And there He looks around at everything.
That's it, baker. Since it was already late, Jesus "…went out to Bethany with the Twelve." (Mark 11:11) He looks around at everything first, and then He heads out. And the story isn't over yet.

Not quite, friend. The text says that since it was already late, Jesus "…went out to Bethany with the Twelve." (Mark 11:11) He heads out of the temple courts instead of staying. And the story isn't over yet.

Jericho isn't in this verse, baker. Mark says that since it was already late, Jesus "…went out to Bethany with the Twelve." (Mark 11:11) Bethany is where He heads, and the Twelve are who the text names as going with Him. And the story isn't over yet.
